_readme: The nightly routine (pf-seo-article, unattended run) takes the first row without `done`, writes that article in that locale, commits, publishes, and marks the row done. Order: Dutch clusters first, then Italian (pillar first), then English (pillar first). Pillar mentions are the exact sentence in the live pillar that announces the cluster; the run turns it into a link. Edit freely; keep the field names.

rows.title_hint: Peuter wil niet eten: wat werkt, wat averechts werkt en wanneer je hulp zoekt
rows.topic: Why toddlers stop eating (growth slows at 1 to 2, autonomy at 2 to 3, fear of new foods), what works (fixed meal moments, small portions, no snacks or drinks right before, eat together, count the week not the meal), what backfires (forcing, the clean plate, dessert as a bribe, screens, cooking twice), the red flags that mean the consultatiebureau or huisarts.
rows.pillar_mention: Dit onderwerp krijgt zijn eigen artikel, net als de vraag wat je doet als je peuter juist groente en fruit laat staan.

rows.title_hint: Hoe vaak moet een kind iets proeven voordat het lekker wordt?
keywords: hoe vaak moet een kind iets proeven
rows.topic: The number honestly (8 to 15, sometimes more; a lick counts, a bite that comes back out counts), why it works (Birch 1982, Wardle 2003), the Voedingscentrum Leren-lusten-plan at home step by step, a sticker or a tick for tasting and never for a clean plate (Cooke 2011, and the Voedingscentrum's reservation, said honestly), how to count without it becoming a project (a chart on the fridge, the app as the counter), what to do when the count stalls.
rows.pillar_mention: Hoe je telt zonder dat het een project wordt, en waarom de teller belangrijker is dan de portie, krijgt een eigen artikel, met een proefkaart om op de koelkast te hangen.

rows.title_hint: Moeilijke eter: wat het is, wat het niet is en hoe je het bord langzaam breder maakt
rows.topic: What a "moeilijke eter" is and is not (a parent's word, not a diagnosis; normal at 2 to 6 versus the signs that need the consultatiebureau or huisarts: weight, fewer than about 20 foods, whole groups missing, gagging or panic), the causes in parent words, widening the plate one taste at a time (one food at a time, next to a safe food, no pressure), what backfires, the tasting count.
rows.pillar_mention: Wat normaal is en wat niet, komt uitgebreider aan bod in een eigen artikel over de moeilijke eter.

rows.title_hint: Peuter eet geen groente: portie, textuur, de dip rond twee jaar en wat wel werkt
keywords: peuter eet geen groente en fruit
rows.topic: Toddler and vegetables: portions (a piece, not a scoop), textures (raw versus cooked, crunchy versus soft), the dip around two years (a toddler who ate everything and stops), which vegetables to start with, fruit as a section (a toddler who also refuses fruit), what works at the table, when to ask the consultatiebureau.
rows.pillar_mention: Dit onderwerp krijgt zijn eigen artikel, net als de vraag wat je doet als je peuter juist groente en fruit laat staan.

rows.title_hint: Welke groente vinden kinderen lekker? De 20 makkelijkste om mee te beginnen
rows.topic: The 20 easiest vegetables to start with (sweet, mild, crunchy: wortel, komkommer, mais, doperwten, paprika, cherrytomaat, zoete aardappel and so on), why children take to them (sweetness, crunch, no bitterness), how to serve each (raw, a dip, roasted), the ones to keep for later (bitter and soft), how the same vegetable changes with the cut and the cooking. Later fed by Project Food tasting data.
rows.pillar_mention: De lijst met de twintig makkelijkste groenten en hoe je ze op tafel zet, volgt als eigen artikel.

rows.title_hint: Groente verstoppen: mag dat, en de ene regel die het proeven redt
rows.topic: Hiding feeds the belly, tasting teaches the tongue: do both. Five ways to hide (in the sauce, in the soup, blended, grated into mince, in the smoothie) and the one rule to keep: always one visible piece next to the plate, the tasting piece. Why hiding alone does not teach a child to eat vegetables, and how to combine it with the tasting count.
rows.pillar_mention: Vijf manieren om te verstoppen en de ene regel om vol te houden, volgen in een eigen artikel.

rows.title_hint: Voedselneofobie: normaal tussen 2 en 6, en zo ga je ermee om
rows.topic: Definition in parent words (the reluctance to eat new foods), the ages 2 to 6, why it exists (evolution, autonomy, bitter sensitivity), how it differs from being a moeilijke eter, what helps (repeated exposure, modelling, no pressure, the same food many times), what makes it worse, that it passes for most children (Dovey 2008), when to ask for help.
rows.pillar_mention: Over de naam en de fase volgt een eigen artikel.

rows.title_hint: Come far mangiare le verdure ai bambini, senza battaglie

perché i bambini non mangiano le verdure
rows.topic: The playbook: refusal is normal (neofobia, 2 to 6), 8 to 15 assaggi, no pressure, reward the tasting not the plate, eat together, the one question after dinner. Sections: quante volte assaggiare (with the counting idea), premi, verdure nascoste (the stance: hide and always one visible piece), quali verdure piacciono, the two-year dip, quando parlare con il pediatra. One announcement sentence per planned Italian cluster (il bambino non mangia, selettività alimentare, neofobia alimentare) so later runs can link them.

rows.title_hint: How many times does a child need to try a new food? The 10 to 15 rule, explained honestly
keywords: how many times does a child need to try a new food
how to get a picky eater to try new foods
cdc picky eating repeated exposure new foods
rows.topic: The AAP and CDC number explained honestly (AAP 'as many as 10 or more', CDC '8 to 10', trials used 12 to 14; we say 8 to 15, sometimes more; a lick counts), what an exposure is, why it works (Birch 1982, Wardle 2003, Cooke 2011), how to count tastes with a chart and the app, a sticker for the taste and never for the plate, what to do when the count stalls.
